deities: Margabandeeswarar (Vazhithunai Nathar — Shiva, swayambhu leaning lingam)
festivals: Kadai Gnayiru (Theerthavari on the last Sunday of Karthigai — the temple's most famous festival)
Panguni (March-April): the sun's rays fall on the lingam — Bhaskara Kshetra

history.dynasty: Chola (13th century); later additions/renovations by Vijayanagara rulers (19th-20th century renovations also recorded)
history.summary: Sri Margabandeeswarar Temple at Virinchipuram is the famous Shiva temple on the southern bank of the Palar river, about 14 km west of Vellore city (sources vary: 13-18 km). CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV town 'Vellore' is the district/city; the actual town is Virinchipuram, Vellore district. History: built in the 13th century by Chola kings (inscriptions of Raja Raja Chola and Rajendra Chola recorded; one review also credits Pallava, Hoysala and Vijayanagara additions — the Pallava claim is chronologically odd and unverified). The name Vazhithunai Nathar means 'the Lord who guides the path'. Legend: Siva Sharma (Brahma, born as a Brahmin to redeem his lie) offered abhishekam; Shiva bent down to help the small boy, hence the lingam's leaning (sliding) form. The temple is the birthplace of the 16th-century Vedic scholar Appayya Dikshitar, who composed the Margabandhu Stotram here (recited for protection during travel); Arunagirinathar also sang of Murugan here. One of the Bhaskara Kshetrams, where the sun's rays fall on the lingam in Panguni. Sthala vriksham: palm tree (said to bear black fruits one year and white the next); theerthams: Simha, Sooli and Brahma.

name: Sri Margabandeeswarar Temple
town_description: Virinchipuram is a village in Vellore district, about 14 km west of Vellore city (sources vary: 13-18 km), on the southern bank of the Palar river near the Chennai-Bengaluru highway (NH 48).

travel.railway: Vellore Town / Vellore Cantt — about 13-15 km; Katpadi Junction — about 15 km (verify).
travel.road: On Virinchipuram Road off the Chennai-Bengaluru highway (NH 48); from the Vellore bypass, about 15 km to Sedhuvalai junction, then right 1 km to Virinjipuram. Autos/taxis from Vellore city; some public buses.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; Karthigai (November-December) for the famous Kadai Gnayiru festival (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM to 11:00 AM; 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM (verify locally). Entry free.
